Decisions.Intro: In startups and ground-up builds, the right decisions matter more than any specific framework.

Items.ApiBoundaries: API contracts, integration boundaries, and service responsibilities.
Items.AuthModels: Authentication and access models (JWT, OAuth2, 2FA, RBAC).
Items.DataModeling: Data models and multi-tenant database schemas.
Items.DeliveryPlanning: Delivery planning, iterations, and realistic release mapping.
Items.FeatureScope: Feature scope and priorities for each release.
Items.PerformanceCost: Performance and cost tradeoffs across infrastructure and design.
Items.ServiceDesign: Service decomposition, modularity, and when to avoid premature microservices.
Items.UxAlignment: Aligning user flows with technical constraints and timelines.

Patterns.Intro: Some of the recurring patterns I use when guiding products and teams.

Items.ArchForIteration: Architect for iteration, not for a hypothetical version 10.
Items.DecisionLogs: Write decisions down instead of relying on memory or chat history.
Items.DocAsProduct: Treat documentation and decision logs as part of the product.
Items.MvpMlp: MVP to MLP: aim for a Minimum Lovable Product, not just a checklist MVP.
Items.PairingOnboarding: Use pairing and real tasks to onboard developers.
Items.ProductMetrics: Care more about product and user metrics than vanity numbers.
Items.UserFeedback: Integrate real user feedback into future iterations.

Patterns.Title: Patterns I apply often

CalmFirstActLater.Body: I try not to react instantly. I pause, understand, and then respond — whether it’s about progress, blockers, or disagreements.
CalmFirstActLater.Title: Calm first, act later

PrepareClarifyExecute.Body: I don’t improvise critical decisions. I write things down, map options, and move once there is enough clarity.
PrepareClarifyExecute.Title: Prepare, clarify, execute

ScalabilityEarly.Body: Multi-tenant schemas, modular services, and maintainable structures are not add-ons — they are part of the first design.
ScalabilityEarly.Title: Think about scalability early

StructureOutlivesUrgency.Body: I document, structure, and organize even when I’m the only one looking at it — because systems outlive the moment.
StructureOutlivesUrgency.Title: Structure outlives urgency

Juniors.Expectation: Junior devs will figure it out.
Juniors.Navigation: Be proactive in mentoring, pairing, and setting clear learning paths.

Mvp.Navigation: Design for iteration, not throwaway prototypes.
Mvp.Reality: MVP decisions shape v2 and v3.

Scope.Navigation: Keep scope flexible, document decisions, and reprioritize often.
Scope.Reality: New information and constraints appear every week.

Tech.Navigation: Evaluate options through product, team, and long-term needs.
Tech.Reality: Wrong choices limit runway and velocity.

Ux.Navigation: Collaborate closely, adjust flows, and protect core usability.
Ux.Reality: UX evolves while features are being built.

Home.About: I’m a Jordan-based senior software engineer with 10+ years of experience building scalable, maintainable, and product-driven web platforms. I’ve grown from frontend foundations into full-stack execution and technical leadership — balancing clean code, system architecture, and user-centric design. My current focus revolves around JavaScript/TypeScript ecosystems, with hands-on depth in React, Next.js, NestJS, and Node backends. Most of my work has been with fast-moving startups, but I’ve also delivered for SMEs and larger organizations across EdTech, SaaS, and internal tooling domains. Beyond coding, I contribute to architectural planning, mentor developers, collaborate with product teams, and help early companies turn ideas into reliable software. Curiosity, clarity, and collaborative problem-solving drive my approach to engineering.
